issue.title: bug(perf): angular2/upgrade keeps running $rootScope.apply() if watchers call setTimeout
issue.body:
I'm trying to upgrade an existing angular1 app to angular2 using the `angular2/upgrade` functionality.

I have noticed that after using `angular2/upgrade` to bootstrap the app, I'm now getting angular1 digests on every single tick, and it tracks down to this line (discovered using the CPU profiler):

``` javascript
this.componentScope.$watch(() => this.changeDetector && this.changeDetector.detectChanges());
```

https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/56a254e6a5674ff928abf96942ec6ef7bc3f0528/modules/angular2/src/upgrade/downgrade_ng2_adapter.ts#L103

I have an angular2 pipe that is configured as `pure: false` and its `transform` method seems to be executed on every single tick of the page. And since I'm using it inside an `*ngFor` and there are a lot of them on the page, the browser becomes unusable.

Here's a trace using Chrome's profiler

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/697707/12091287/9adca2ac-b2fe-11e5-9e85-1d5737c8fb06.png)

Am I doing something wrong or is this a bug?

EDIT: Repro at https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/6245#issuecomment-168732222

issue.title: When upgrading from angular1, updating a $watched value from a setTimeout ends up outside ngZone
[upgrade-adapter-rc.4] change detection does not work sometime on a hybrid app
issue.body:
**I'm submitting a ...**  (check one with "x")

```
[ X ] bug report
```

On a hybrid application (mixture of ng1 and ng2), change detection doesn't work sometime

**Current behavior**
In `upgrade_adapter.ts`:

``` javascript
ngZone.onMicrotaskEmpty.subscribe({
                        next: (_: any) => ngZone.runOutsideAngular(() => rootScope.$evalAsync())
                      });
```

**Expected/desired behavior**
If I change this to: 

``` javascript
ngZone.onMicrotaskEmpty.subscribe({
                        next: (_: any) => ngZone.run(() => rootScope.$evalAsync())
                      });
```

Change detection seems to work.

One drawback is: this will re-introduce the infinite `$rootScope.$digest` (https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/6385)

**Reproduction of the problem**
Unfortunately I haven't been able to replicate the issue on plunker, it only happens on a specific situation I have on one of my production servers.

But hopefully someone who is familiar with the codes above, can give me a light on what can affect this code, and I will give another go at replicating the issue on plunker.

Thanks guys! 

**What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior?**
To make hybrid application possible
- **Angular version:** 2.0.0-rc.4
- **Browser:** Chrome 51.0.2704.106
- **Language:** TypeScript 1.8 | ES6

issue.title: fix(upgrade): detect async downgrade component changes

labels.name: action: merge
labels.description: The PR is ready for merge by the caretaker

issue.body:
This commit effectively reverts 7e0f02f96e59863dff563cb7036c21aa58220a67
as it was an invalid fix for #6385, that created a more significant
bug, which was that changes were not always being detected.

Angular 1 digests should be run inside the ngZone to ensure
that async changes are detected.

We don't know how to fix #6385 without breaking change detection
at this stage. That issue is triggered by async operations, such as
`setTimeout`, being triggered inside scope watcher functions.

One could argue that watcher functions should be pure and not do
work such as triggering async operations. It is possible that the
original use case could be supported by moving the debounce
logic into the watch listener function, which is only called if the
watched value actually changes.

Closes #10660, #12318, #12034

It is possible that this revert could be considered a breaking change since
the previous bug is now apparent again.

The same fix will need to be done on `upgrade/static` as well, once this is approved.
